content:
https://grothendieck.commutator.io/

Hi I started a bit of the Grothendieck handwritten notes just for fun, with my remaining Claude credits every week and have pretty good results.

I have LaTex file both in form of raw notes and modernized maths. Do you think it could be interesting to have a pipeline to transform LaTeX to LEAN and actually prove some of the assertions ?

Still using Claude Code, I also build a small website to help mathematicians "debug" the transcription more easily.

I am currently a data/AI engineer with a STEM background. I estimate it could take a year if I do this all by myself with a small budget, but can also write a batch pipeline using the Claude API.

Wow what a beautiful collection. Some of these diagrams absolutely blow me away.

Michel Hua said:

Do you think it could be interesting to have a pipeline to transform LaTeX to LEAN and actually prove some of the assertions ?

I'd love to know if you made any progress on this. There are now many popular frameworks to do this sort of thing.

Hi Jack,
I used these Claude skills https://github.com/cameronfreer/lean4-skills
plus some homemade skills for math rewriting and bibliography search.

Since the documents were actually fragments and not fully written originally.

I am almost finished with a PDF file that is supposed to contain only novelties.

I was also thinking of splitting it and sending it to area specialists for quick review. Would your lab be interested in proof reading some of them?

Sorry that the document is in French.

Do you know a better way ?
It’s fascinating to see something like this after only ever looking at dull code. Personally, I’m actually really curious about how the UI was designed.

Hi @Yoonwoo Jeong ,
If by "dull code" you mean the LEAN source code was badly written sorry for that.

It also shows how easy it was formalizing proofs was for Anthropic and OpenAI recently, the only thing that's missing to try the harder conjectures is obviously only Claude token budget on my side. I would say the project only had cost 200 USD and several week ends chatting with Claude.

I had the intuition in August that LLM were powerful enough through these aspects and wanted to try solving the transcription challenge, which I learned about 7 years ago in a pop science Youtube video:

  • multimodal LLM had good performance in OCR and computer vision
  • reasoning capabilities and at maths in the benchmarks
  • ability to fill out gaps in fragmented sentences and find most probable formulation

You can see from my first post in Zulip that I also tried in parallel at that time to rewrite high school maths in LEAN.

For the UI it's a frontend only application, I am mostly expert in data engineering and have basic skills in developing and deploying web applications.
But how you initiate it with a coding assistant is basically telling it which framework to use, and how you want things to be presented, and setup all the CI/CD automation in your repo, which is what professional software engineers like me usually do at work. Part of the web application design is just taken care of by Claude Code without you expliciting. I invite you to try on a personal project even non scientific.

And I also reused my skills of when I was a maths student 15 years ago, where I learned the basics of writing scientific articles with LaTeX.

It you need to design a customized web-based simulation interface for your scientific research, you can also think of designing experiments using numerical analysis algorithms.
Here is a basic one for GPS https://tipe.commutator.io/geometrie/

Another thing that struck me through the process, is that people are now being able to write maths and initiate a research subject just using bribes of ideas. If you look at the document the LLM was able to perform bibliographical research on post Grothendieck mathematics and cross over 87 references.

Hi, @Michel Hua , Thanks for your thoughtful response. I, too, find it regrettable that older materials from the past have not been properly organized or formatted for the present. Your initiative serves as a great source of inspiration. In particular, since it seems like a way to overcome the limitations often encountered with foreign-language materials, I intend to give it a try myself.

Formalizing also has a potential benefit of correcting mistakes. Notes have lots of tests and counter-examples that the final text doesn't have.

See this post on MathOverflow where the author of a classical textbook answered to me, following my investigations.

We could indeed continue with other archives from mathematicians, that are kept by national libraries. I submitted the idea to BnF and IHP in France.

That is a truly fascinating case. It’s amazing that the author replied personally! Beyond mathematics, I am also considering the formalization of topics in analytic philosophy—such as semantics within modal logic. I’m not sure how well it will turn out, though.

It depends if the area your investigating already has researchers working on it. You will need LLM to perform bibliography search and confront facts at some point.

What you are describing looks more like the area of "digital humanities".

I also tried that here as a smaller problem to start with and develop techniques. Here is the same kind of work but for Edward Hopper notebooks, https://hopper.commutator.io/

There is no math, mostly art referencing and accounting but I used Lean to balance the ledgers.

(Please note Whitney museum website is also down today because of the global PHP cybersecurity issues, I in fact learned that a lot are using Omeka PHP CMS to host the archives)

My position relies somewhat more on formal logic. https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/counterfactuals/
The issues with PHP are deeply concerning. While one would hope for serious attention to security patches, it is highly likely that the reality will be quite the opposite.

Looks interesting, I didn't know about causal decision theory.
Apparently there are archives from Leibniz you could transcribe, as he was one of the main philosopher/mathematician to try to conceptualize this.
There are also text from René Descartes obviously a bit before him.

Antique greek text corpus are one github and philologists / digital humanists are already studying them using NLP and now LLM.

The lean-skills technique above should work, but I have no idea the kind of objects you who manipulate in Lean to modelize the reasoning of these philosophers. AlgebraicTopology, GroupTheory, ProbabilityTheory ? The different APIs would have to be built?

https://github.com/yoonwoojeong/SEP-Counterfactuals.git I am currently working on this. I want to focus on educational objectives, and I don’t think a dependency on Mathlib is necessary. While the works of the classical philosophers you mentioned are certainly significant, they sometimes lack the level of rigor expected in a modern context.

As for the Greek philosophers, I actually tried to learn the Greek language myself—just to verify things—but I found it truly difficult.
